name: chuul
languages: understands Deep Speech but can't speak

special_abilities.name: amphibious
special_abilities.desc: The chuul can breathe air and water.

special_abilities.name: sense magic
special_abilities.desc: The chuul senses magic within 120 feet of it at will. This trait otherwise works like the detect magic spell but isn't itself magical.

actions.name: multiattack
actions.desc: The chuul makes two pincer attacks. If the chuul is grappling a creature, the chuul can also use its tentacles once.

actions.name: pincer
actions.desc: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage. The target is grappled (escape DC 14) if it is a Large or smaller creature and the chuul doesn't have two other creatures grappled.

actions.name: tentacles
actions.desc: One creature grappled by the chuul must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or be poisoned for 1 minute. Until this poison ends, the target is paralyzed. The target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

lore:
Deep within the brackish mires and the salt-crusted ruins of fallen empires dwells the Chuul—a nightmare of chitin and cold, calculating instinct. These crustaceous horrors are the silent sentinels of the marsh, blending seamlessly with the decay until a traveler wanders too close to the water’s edge.

The Chuul is no mere beast; it is a methodical predator. It strikes with massive, serrated pincers, yet its true terror lies in the writhing mass of tentacles masking its mandibles. These appendages secrete a numbing ichor that freezes the blood, leaving the victim conscious but immobile as they are dragged into the lightless depths to be consumed at leisure.

Local folklore speaks of the Chuul as the "Grave-Keepers of the Sunken Gods." It is whispered that they do not hunt for hunger alone, but to hoard relics of arcane power for masters who vanished eons ago. To find a Chuul is to find the threshold of a buried secret, though few survive the encounter. Should you hear the rhythmic clacking of shears amidst the reeds, turn back; the marsh remembers what the world has forgotten.
